chapter: Studio recordings of the late twenties and thirties
title: The Dorsey Brothers Concert Orchestra and Eugene Ormandy
summary: Kline reads the 1928 Okeh Dorsey Brothers sessions conducted by Ormandy, which Morehouse recalls only vaguely.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You were impressed then. Okay. And then you made some records with the Dorsey brothers.
Yeah.
"Mary Ann and Persian Rug". Do you remember that one? Carl Kress was on guitar.
Yeah.
Your friend. You wouldn't remember the Dorsey Brothers orchestra?
No.
No, okay. And there is something else unusual. Dorsey Brothers Concert Orchestra conducted by Dr. Eugene Ormandy.
Eugene Ormandy.
Do you remember playing under Eugene Ormandy?
No.

You did. You made a record. The Dorsey Brothers Concert Orchestra recorded for Okeh records, July 16, 1928. Well maybe you didn't play with him. There was Manny Klein, Hal Kemp, Skinny Ennis, some others. Maybe you weren't on the date.
Yeah

Maybe you weren't. Because the people kept coming and going. The Dorsey Brothers orchestra kept adding and dropping people. Let me see. You did play with the Dorsey Brothers Concert Orchestra. Yes, I think maybe you did. Fuzzy Farrar, Phil Napoleon, Glenn Miller, Eddie Lang. You made 'Lover Come Back To Me', part one and part two. Do you remember that record? Do you remember that? You don't remember that. 'Lover Come Back To Me.'
Yes.
You do? Do you remember Eugene Ormandy? You don't remember him.
Eugene Ormandy, yes I remember him.
He was your conductor.
Yeah.
Did you have any impressions? Do you remember anything about the way he conducted a jazz band?
No, no.
